ig_carousel_topic.topic: The Kelly criterion — explained without the math degree
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much should you actually bet?

Most bettors guess. Kelly gives you a framework.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common mistake:
betting the same flat amount on every play regardless of edge or odds.

A 60% edge at -110 is not the same as a 54% edge at +200. Treating them the same costs you money over time.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Kelly's insight: bet a percentage of your bankroll proportional to your edge.

Bigger edge + better odds = bigger bet.
Smaller edge = smaller bet.
No edge = no bet.

Size follows the math, not the hype.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Simple example:
You have a 56% win probability on a -110 line.
Full Kelly says bet about 6% of your bankroll.

Most sharp bettors use Half Kelly (3% here) to reduce variance while keeping the edge working.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
You don't need a formula tattooed on your arm.
Just ask: 'Am I betting more when my edge is bigger?'

If yes, you're already thinking the right way.
Save this — it's worth revisiting.
